Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

exhaust verb

use up completely

also use up, drain, deplete, run through (money), exhaust supplies, exhausted (used up), inexhaustible

classical

Cic. Vat. 5: aerārium (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 4.2.7: amīcōrum benignitās exhausta est (Lewis & Short)

exhauriō, exhaurīre, exhausī, exhaustum

verb, fourth conjugation, transitive

drain, empty, exhaust

Literally to draw out a liquid, to bail (sentīnam exhaurīre, Cic. Sen. 17), to drink up; then to empty a treasury, a province, a people of its money, and to use up anything: patience, kindness, a subject. It also means to undergo, to see through (labōrēs exhaurīre, Liv.).

Other words

  • cōnsūmō, cōnsūmere, cōnsūmpsī, cōnsūmptum — use up, consume

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 6: patrimōnium per luxuriam (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.G. 6.43: frūmenta (Lewis & Short)

    To use up, spend, eat up (see eat-up): money, time, supplies.

Examples

  • Prōsit, sed nōn exhauriās tōtum.

    Cheers, but don’t drink it all.Schottennius, Confabulātiōnēs, Dē pōtū postrēmō ā cēnā

  • aliī sentīnam exhauriant

    others should bail out the bilgeCic. Sen. 17

See also exhaust, use, eat up, fail, spend.

SourcesLewis & Short: exhaurio · Lewis & Short: consumo

Cicero (Sen. 17) and Schottennius from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-schottenius); Schottennius is sixteenth-century school Latin. The other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
